cloudInstall.title: Installing the App in the Cloud
cloudInstall.subtitle: Cloud deployment planning, readiness, and validation workbench for WLWAI

overview.missionText: This module helps you plan, prepare, and validate the cloud deployment of Workplace Learning With AI. Use it as a deployment workbench — not a static README. Work through each section, tick the checklists, and confirm the deployment is solid before going live.

readiness.architectureDetail: Cloud stack selected: Vercel + Cloud Run + Atlas + Firebase
readiness.envSecretsDetail: Review all .env variables and map them to cloud secrets
readiness.frontendDeployDetail: Deploy React app to Vercel and validate from the cloud
readiness.backendDeployDetail: Deploy FastAPI to Google Cloud Run with correct secrets
readiness.dataAuthDetail: Connect MongoDB Atlas and verify Firebase Auth in production
readiness.smokeTestsDetail: Run all critical smoke tests and confirm the deployment is working

workflow.step1: Read the architecture recommendation (Target Architecture tab)
workflow.step2: Confirm which services to keep and which to defer
workflow.step3: Map all environment variables to cloud secrets (Env & Secrets tab)
workflow.step4: Deploy the React frontend to Vercel
workflow.step5: Deploy the FastAPI backend to Google Cloud Run
workflow.step6: Connect MongoDB Atlas and verify MONGO_URI
workflow.step7: Verify Firebase Auth works in production
workflow.step8: Run the smoke test checklist and confirm everything works

arch.principleText: Do not rewrite the stack. The correct strategy is to cloudify the current architecture incrementally. The cloud version should feel like the same product — not a rebuilt product.
arch.deferredTitle: Deferred to Phase 2 (do not include in v1)
arch.deferredDesc: These services are intentionally excluded from the first deployment to keep scope manageable. Add them after the core deployment is stable.

budgetTiers.starter: $29–59/mo — M2 Atlas + Vercel Pro + small Cloud Run

notes: n8n is intentionally deferred to phase 2+
websearch-backend is optional and can be deployed separately later
Start with free tiers; upgrade only when needed
Vercel and Cloud Run both support custom domains

frontend.name: React Frontend
frontend.desc: Deploy the React frontend to Vercel. Connect via GitHub for automatic CI/CD on every push to main.
frontend.why: Vercel is the natural fit for a React frontend. It provides GitHub-based deployments, a free tier, edge CDN, custom domains, and a zero-configuration build pipeline for React applications.

backend.name: FastAPI Backend
backend.desc: Deploy the FastAPI backend as a container on Google Cloud Run. Serverless, auto-scaling, and billed per request.
backend.why: Cloud Run is ideal for the existing FastAPI backend. It is container-first (the repo already has a Dockerfile), scales to zero when idle, and integrates natively with Google Cloud Secret Manager for secrets.

database.name: MongoDB
database.desc: Move MongoDB to Atlas for a fully managed, globally available database with backups and monitoring.
database.why: MongoDB Atlas is the natural continuation of the current MongoDB-based design. It requires minimal application changes — just a new MONGO_URI connection string. The free M0 tier is sufficient for initial deployment.

auth.name: Authentication
auth.desc: Keep Firebase Auth as-is. No migration needed. Configure production domains and backend service account.
auth.why: Firebase Auth is already integrated in both frontend and backend. There is no reason to migrate it. The only production change needed is adding the Vercel domain to Firebase Authorized Domains and ensuring the backend service account is set in Cloud Run.

dns.name: DNS & SSL
dns.desc: Add Cloudflare for DNS management, SSL termination, and optional DDoS protection after core deployment is stable.
dns.why: Cloudflare provides free DNS management, SSL, and a global edge network. It is recommended for Phase 2 after the core deployment is working, to avoid adding unnecessary complexity in the first rollout.

env.infoText: SECRET variables must never be committed to git or exposed in the browser. They go into Cloud Run Secret Manager (backend) or stay server-side. PUBLIC variables are safe to include in the build (e.g. Firebase public config). OPTIONAL variables can be deferred to Phase 2.

smoke.automatedDesc: Run real checks against backend endpoints, environment variables, and service connectivity
